    #The Standard Atmosphere

    P=ρRT where R=287.058 J/kg⋅K

    Standard mean sea level (MSL) conditions:

    • p0​=101325 Pa
    • ρ0​=1.225 kg/m3
    • T0​=288.16 K (15°C)
    • a0​=340.294 m/s
    • g0​=9.80665 m/s2

    Relevant unit conversions:

    • 1 ft=0.3048 m
    • 1 kt=1.852 km/h

    #Pressure and Density Variation

    Gradient Region (0 km < h < 11 km)

    p0​p​=(T0​T​)−aRg0​​

    ρ0​ρ​=(T0​T​)−aRg0​​−1

    T=T0​+a(h−h0​)

    Isothermal Region (11 km < h < 20 km)

    p1​p​=e−RTg0​​(h−h1​)

    ρ1​ρ​=e−RTg0​​(h−h1​)

    where h0​=0 km

    T0​=288.16 K

    p0​=101325 Pa

    ρ0​=1.225 kg/m3

    a=−0.0065 K/m

    where h1​=11000 m

    T=216.65 K

    p1​=22632.1 Pa

    ρ1​=0.36391 kg/m3

    #Flight Speed and Mach Number

    Local speed of sound:

    Mach number:

    Density ratio:

    a=γRT​ where γ=cv​cp​​=1.4 (for air)

    M=aV​ where V is aircraft’s airspeed

    σ=ρ0​ρ∞​​

    Pitot-Static Tube

    p1​+21​ρV1​2=p2​+21​ρV2​2

    V∞​=ρ∞​2(ptot​−p∞​)​​

    Types of Airspeed

    Indicated airspeed:

    Calibrated airspeed:

    Equivalent airspeed:

    True airspeed:

    Vi​ (instrument error, air compressibility error, air density error)

    Vc​=Vi​+ΔV (corrected for position/installation error)

    Ve​=Vi​+ΔV (corrected for compressibility of air)

    V∞​=Ve​ρ∞​ρ0​​​ (corrected for air density error)

    Ground Speed

    Vg​=V∞​−Vheadwind​ (reduces takeoff run)

    Vg​=V∞​+Vtailwind​ (reduces flight time)

    #Review of Aerodynamics

    #Lift and Drag (Airfoil)

    Shear stress in a flow:

    τ=μdydv​=δ2μV∞​​

    where δ is boundary layer thickness

    Symmetrical airfoil:

    Cl​=Clα​α

    Cambered airfoil:

    Cl​=Clα​(α−α0​)

    Flap Effectiveness

    Lift coefficient with flaps deployed:

    Cl​=Clα​(α−α0​+τδf)

    τ=dδfdCl​​⋅dCl​dα​=dδfdα​

    where τ is flap effectiveness
    and     δf is degree of flap deflection

    #Lift and Drag (Wing)

    Induced drag of a wing:

    CDi​​=kCL​2=πeARCL​2​

    Lift curve slope of a wing:

    a=dαdCL​​=1+πeARa0​​a0​​

    where a0​ is the lift curve slope of the airfoil

    Compressibility Corrections

    For AR>4:

    Incompressible flow: a=1+πeARa0​​a0​​

    Subsonic flow: a=1−M∞​2​+πeARa0​​a0​​

    Supersonic flow: a=M∞​2−1​4​

    For AR<4:

    Incompressible flow: a=1+[πARa0​​]2​+πARa0​​a0​​

    Subsonic flow: a=1−M∞​2+[πARa0​​]2​+πARa0​​a0​​

    Supersonic flow: a=M∞​2−1​4​(1−2ARM∞​2−1​1​)

    #Lift and Drag (Aircraft)

    Total drag of an aircraft:

    CD​=CD0​​+CDi​​+CDwave​​

    D=21​ρV2SCD​

    where q=21​ρV2S

    Drag/thrust required:

    D=TR​=q(CD0​​+kCL​2)

    D=TR​=AV2+V2B​

    where A=21​ρSCD0​​ and B=21​ρSkW2​

    Speed at which drag is minimum:

    VDmin​​=ρS2W​CD0​​k​​​

    Minimum drag speed at a given altitude:

    Vh​=V0​σ1​​

    where V0​ is the minimum drag speed at sea level

    Maximum lift-to-drag ratio:

    DL​max​=2kCD0​​​1​

    Minimum drag of an aircraft:

    Dmin​=2LkCD0​​​=2WkCD0​​​

    Note that CD0​​=kCL​2 for minimum drag.
    Minimum drag is constant with respect to altitude.

    #Review of Propulsion

    #Jet

    T=mair​(Vjet​−V∞​)+mfuel​Vjet​

    Propulsive efficiency of a jet:

    ηp​=1+V∞​Vjet​​2​

    #Propeller

    T=21​ρA(Vs​2−V∞​2)

    Propulsive efficiency of a propeller:

    ηp​=1+V∞​Vs​​2​

    Thrust Generation of Turboprop

    Propeller efficiency:

    ηpr​=Pshaft​Pprop​​

    Total propulsive power:

    P=ηpr​Pes​

    where Pes​ is equivalent shaft power, which is total power including jet thrust

    #Level Flight Performance

    #Power Required

    Lift coefficient for which power is minimum:

    3CD0​​=kCL​2

    CLPmin​​​=k3CD0​​​​

    Speed at which power is minimum:

    VPmin​​=ρS2W​3CD0​​k​​​

    Minimum power required:

    PRmin​​=ρS2W3​​(CL​3/2CD​​)Pmin​​

    #Level Flight

    Turbojet aircraft:

    T0​T​=σm

    Thrust is constant with flight speed.
    m≈1 for turbojet aircraft.

    Turboprop aircraft:

    P0​P​=σn

    Power is constant with flight speed.
    n≈0.7 for turboprop aircraft.

    Level Flight for Jet Aircraft

    Thrust available at a given altitude:

    TA​=T0​⋅σm

    Minimum and maximum flight speeds occur at points where TA​=TR​.

    Vmin/max​=[2ATA​±(TA​)2−4AB​​ ]21​

    Vmin/max​=ρCD0​​(WTA​​)(SW​)±SW​(WTA​​)2−4kCD0​​​​​

    Note that at absolute ceiling, Vmin​=Vmax​=VDmin​​.

    Expressions for A and B:

    A=21​ρSCD0​​

    B=21​ρSkW2​

    Absolute ceiling (density altitude):

    ρ=ρ0​(T0​Dmin​​)m1​

    where T0​ is thrust available at sea level

    #Climb Performance

    #Equilibrium Equations

    θ=γ+α

    where θ is pitch angle,
    γ is flight path (climb) angle,
    α is angle of attack of aircraft

    L=Wcosγ

    T=D+Wsinγ

    R/C=Vsinγ

    Load factor for climb:

    n=cosγ

    Rearranging the equilibrium equations:

    R/C=WV(T−D)​

    SEP=WPA​−PR​​

    sinγ=WT−D​

    sinγ=VSEP​

    where SEP is specific excess power expressed in W/N

    #Maximum Climb Rate (Graphical)

    Plotting the graph:

    • Calculate Vmin​ and Vmax​ for the chosen altitude
    • Calculate PA​ and PR​ for the range Vmin​≤V≤Vmax​
    • Calculate SEP for the range Vmin​≤V≤Vmax​
    • Plot SEP against flight speed V

    Jet Aircraft

    PA​=TA​V=(TA​σm)V

    PR​=TR​V=(AV2+V2B​)V

    Propeller Aircraft

    PA​=ηpr​(P0​σm)

    PR​=TR​V=(AV2+V2B​)V

    #Maximum Climb Rate (Analytical)

    General equation for climb rate:

    R/C=Vsinγ=V[WT​−21​W/SρV2CD0​​​−SW​(ρV22k​)]

    Jet Aircraft

    Speed at which climb rate is maximum:

    VR/Cmax​​=3ρCD0​​Z(WT​)(SW​)​​

    Z=1+1+(DL​max​)2(WT​)23​​

    Maximum climb rate:

    R/Cmax​=3ρCD0​​(W/S)Z​​(WT​)23​[1−6Z​−2(T/W)2(L/D)max2​Z3​]

    Propeller Aircraft

    Speed at which climb rate is maximum:

    VR/Cmax​​=VPmin​​=ρS2W​3CD0​​k​​​

    Maximum climb rate:

    R/Cmax​=WPA​​−(L/D)max​1.155​ρS2W​3CD0​​k​​​

    #Maximum Climb Angle

    Jet Aircraft

    Speed at which climb angle is maximum:

    Vγmax​​=VDmin​​=ρS2W​CD0​​k​​​

    Climb angle for jet aircraft is maximum when D is minimum.
    Since     TA​ is constant, minimum D gives highest excess thrust.

    Maximum climb angle:

    γmax​=sin−1(WTA​​−(L/D)max​1​)

    Corresponding climb rate:

    R/Cγmax​​=Vγmax​​sinγmax​

    Propeller Aircraft

    Speed at which climb angle is maximum:

    Vγmax​​=ρ(PA​/W)4k(W/S)​

    Maximum climb angle:

    γmax​=sin−1[4k(W/S)ρ(PA​/W)2​−ρ(PA​/W)28k2(W/S)CD0​​​−8k(W/S)ρ(PA​/W)2​]

    Corresponding climb rate:

    R/Cγmax​​=Vγmax​​sinγmax​

    #Time to Climb

    R/C=Vsinγ=dtdh​

    t=∫0h​R/C1​ dh

    Altitude vs R/C graph is simply the equation of a straight line.
    Express     R/C in terms of h and evaluate the integral.

    #Glide Performance

    #Equilibrium Equations

    θ=γ−α

    where θ is pitch angle,
    γ is flight path (glide) angle,
    α is angle of attack of aircraft

    L=Wcosγ

    D=Wsinγ

    γ=LD​=WD​=Rh​

    Small angle approximation

    Descent rate:

    dtdh​=−Vγ

    dtdh​=−WDV​

    dtdh​=−WPR​​

    #Maximum Range

    Speed at which range is maximum:

    VRmax​​=VDmin​​=ρS2W​CD0​​k​​​

    Maximum range is achieved when γ, and thus D is minimum, since W is constant.

    Maximum range:

    Rmax​=2kCD0​​​h​

    Corresponding glide angle:

    γRmax​​=2kCD0​​​

    Glide angle is expressed in radians.

    Corresponding angle of attack:

    αRmax​​=CLα​CD0​​/k​​+α0​

    Corresponding descent rate:

    dtdh​Rmax​​=−(CD0​​/k)3/423/2CD0​​​ρSW​​

    Corresponding endurance:

    ERmax​​=23/2CD0​​(CD0​​/k)3/4​WS​​∫0h​ρ​ dh

    Expression for ρ can be obtained from standard atmosphere equations.

    #Maximum Endurance

    Speed at which endurance is maximum:

    VEmax​​=VPmin​​=ρS2W​3CD0​​k​​​

    Maximum endurance is achieved when descent rate is minimum.
    Descent rate is minimized when     PR​ is minimum since W is constant.

    Corresponding descent rate:

    dtdh​Emax​​=−(3CD0​​/k)3/425/2CD0​​​ρSW​​

    Maximum endurance:

    Emax​=25/2CD0​​(3CD0​​/k)3/4​WS​​∫0h​ρ​ dh

    Expression for ρ can be obtained from standard atmosphere equations.

    Corresponding glide angle:

    γEmax​​=43kCD0​​​​

    Glide angle is expressed in radians.

    Corresponding angle of attack:

    αEmax​​=CLα​3CD0​​/k​​+α0​

    Corresponding range:

    REmax​​=4h​kCD0​​3​​

    #Comparison of Equations

    Maximum Range

    γRmax​​=γmin​=2kCD0​​​

    dtdh​Rmax​​=−(CD0​​/k)3/423/2CD0​​​ρSW​​

    VRmax​​=VDmin​​=ρS2W​CD0​​k​​​

    Rmax​=2kCD0​​​h​

    ERmax​​=23/2CD0​​(CD0​​/k)3/4​WS​​∫0h​ρ​ dh

    CLRmax​​​=CLDmin​​​=kCD0​​​​

    Maximum Endurance

    γEmax​​=3​2​γRmax​​

    dtdh​Emax​​=33/42​(dtdh​Rmax​​)

    VEmax​​=VPmin​​=31/41​VRmax​​

    REmax​​=23​​Rmax​

    Emax​=233/4​ERmax​​

    CLEmax​​​=CLPmin​​​=k3CD0​​​​

    #Level Turn Performance

    #Equilibrium Equations

    Lcosϕ=W

    cosϕ=n1​

    L=nW

    R=gn2−1​V2​

    ω=Vgn2−1​​

    where ω is expressed in rad/s

    #Minimum Turn Radius

    qRmin​​=T/W2k(W/S)​

    Speed at which turn radius is minimum:

    VRmin​​=ρ(T/W)4k(W/S)​​

    Corresponding load factor:

    nRmin​​=2−(T/W)24kCD0​​​​

    Minimum radius:

    Rmin​=ρg(T/W)1−(T/W)24kCD0​​​​4k(W/S)​

    Note that the smallest possible turn radius is when thrust is at its maximum.

    #Maximum Turn Rate

    Maximum turn rate:

    ωmax​=gW/Sρ​(2kT/W​−kCD0​​​​)​

    Corresponding load factor:

    nωmax​​=kCD0​​​T/W​−1​

    Speed at which turn rate is maximum:

    Vωmax​​=(CD0​​k​)41​ρ2(W/S)​​

    #Pull-Up/Pull-Down Performance

    #Pull-Up Maneuver

    R=g(n−1)V2​

    ω=Vg(n−1)​

    #Pull-Down Maneuver

    R=g(n+1)V2​

    ω=Vg(n+1)​

    #Corner/Maneuver Point

    Vcorner​=ρSCLmax​​2nmax​W​​

    Note that the corner point is the intersection of the stall boundary and structural boundary.
    Thus, the maximum load factor is equal to the limit load factor and where     CL​=CLmax​​.

    #Take-Off Performance

    VLO​=1.1Vstall​

    V2​=1.2Vstall​

    Note that V2​ is also known as the safety speed (to clear a specified height).
    Specified height is 35ft for commercial aircraft and 50ft for military aircraft.

    #Ground Run

    Ground run is the total runway distance from standstill to liftoff.

    Newton’s second law for ground run:

    F=gW​⋅a=T−D−μr​(W−L)

    General equation for ground run:

    sga​=2gW​∫0Vg​​T−D−μr​(W−L)d(Vg​2)​

    Note that Vg​=VLO​ if there is wind.

    Approach 1

    Lift coefficient for ground run (if not given):

    CL​=2kμr​​

    where μr​ is the rolling resistance coefficient

    Corrected profile drag (flap deflection):

    CD0​​=C~D0​​+SW​Kuc​m−0.215

    where Kuc​=5.81×10−5 for zero flap deflection (for takeoff) and
    Kuc​=3.16×10−5 for maximum flap deflection (for landing) and
    C~D0​​ is the uncorrected profile drag coefficient

    Corrected total drag (ground effect):

    CD​=CD0​​+ϕk~CL​2

    CD​=CD0​​+[1+(16h/b)2(16h/b)2​]k~CL​2

    where ϕ is the ground effect correction factor
    and     k~ is the uncorrected Oswald efficiency factor

    Ground run distance:

    sg​=2gKA​1​ln(1+KT​KA​VLO​2​)+NVLO​

    KA​=−2(W/S)ρ​(CD​−μr​CL​)

    KT​=WT​−μr​

    Note that N is the time taken by the aircraft to rotate and liftoff.
    N=3 for commercial (large) aircraft and N=1 for military (small) aircraft.

    Approach 2

    Effective ground speed of aircraft:

    Veff​=2​VLO​​=0.707VLO​

    Effective airspeed of aircraft if there is wind:

    Veff​=Veff(airspeed)​−Vhw​

    Veff​=Veff(airspeed)​+Vtw​

    Ground run distance:

    sg​=2gWVLO​2​[T−D−μr​(W−L)1​]Veff(airspeed)​​+NVLO​

    Note that thrust, drag, and lift are evaluated at the effective airspeed.

    #Flare and Climb (Airborne Distance)

    Flight path of flare and climb:

    R=g6.96Vstall​2​

    Note that flare and climb is analyzed as a pull-up maneuver.

    Speed during flare and climb:

    V=1.15Vstall​

    Lift coefficient during flare and climb:

    CL​=0.9CLmax​​

    Load factor during flare and climb:

    n=1.19

    Airborne distance:

    sa​=2Rhob​−hob​2​

    whereby hob​ is the specified height that the aircraft needs to clear

    #Landing Performance

    Commercial Aircraft

    Va​=1.3Vstall​

    Vf​=1.225Vstall​

    VTD​=1.15Vstall​

    Military Aircraft

    Va​=1.2Vstall​

    Vf​=1.15Vstall​

    VTD​=1.1Vstall​

    #Approach Distance

    Approach angle:

    γa​=WD−T​=L/D1​−WT​

    Distance covered during approach phase:

    sa​=tanγa​15.2−hf​​

    #Flare Distance

    n=1.2

    R=g(n−1)Vf​2​

    where Vf​ is flare speed

    Distance covered during flare phase:

    sf​=Rsinγf​

    Height at which flare is executed:

    hf​=R(1−cosγf​)

    Note that γf​=γa​.

    #Free Roll Distance

    Speed is assumed to be constant and equal to VTD​.

    sfr​=NVTD​

    #Braked Roll Distance

    Effective ground speed of aircraft:

    Veff​=0.707VTD​

    Braked roll distance:

    sbr​=2gWVTD​2​[Trev​+D+μr​(W−L)1​]Veff(airspeed)​​

    Note that reverse thrust, drag, and lift are evaluated at the effective airspeed.

    #Range and Endurance

    Power specific fuel consumption (SFC):

    c=Pb​ expressed in N/W/s

    where b is weight of fuel burnt per second

    Thrust specific fuel consumption (TSFC):

    ct​=Tb​ expressed in N/N/s

    For propeller aircraft, SFC is related to TSFC by:

    c=Vct​ηpr​​

    Definitions of the different aircraft weights:

    • W0​ — gross weight of aircraft (full fuel, payload, and crew)
    • W1​ — weight of aircraft with empty fuel tanks
    • Wf​ — instantaneous weight of fuel
    • W — instantaneous weight of aircraft

    #Propeller Aircraft

    Maximum Range

    Speed at which range is maximum:

    VRmax​​=VDmin​​=ρS2W​CD0​​k​​​

    Maximum range of aircraft:

    Rmax​=cηpr​​2kCD0​​​1​ lnW1​W0​​

    Independent of altitude.

    Maximum Endurance

    Speed at which endurance is maximum:

    VEmax​​=VPmin​​=ρS2W​3CD0​​k​​​

    Maximum endurance of aircraft:

    CD​CL​3/2​max​=41​(kCD0​​1/33​)43​

    Emax​=cηpr​​2ρS​ CD​CL​3/2​max​(W1​​1​−W0​​1​)

    Decreases with altitude.

    #Jet Aircraft

    Maximum Range

    Speed at which range is maximum:

    VRmax​​=VCL​​/CD​max​​=ρS2W​CD0​​3k​​​

    Substitute W0​ and W1​ to obtain the flight speed with initial weight and final weight.

    Maximum range of aircraft:

    CD​CL​​​max​=43​(3kCD0​​31​)41​

    Rmax​=ct​2​ρS2​​CD​CL​​​max​(W0​​−W1​​)

    Increases with altitude.

    Maximum Endurance

    Speed at which endurance is maximum:

    VEmax​​=VDmin​​=ρS2W​CD0​​k​​​

    Maximum endurance of aircraft:

    Emax​=2ct​kCD0​​​1​ lnW1​W0​​

    Independent of altitude.

    #Energy Height Concept

    Energy height of an aircraft:

    He​=h+2gV2​

    Specific excess power (SEP):

    Ps​=dtdh​+gV​atdV​=dtdHe​​
